title: A point isolated in its fibre is quasi-finite on every affine pair (Stacks 01TH, (2) implies (4))
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$ with first projection $p:X_s\to X$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Assume that the unique point $\xi\in X_s$ with $p(\xi)=x$ is isolated in $X_s$, i.e. $\{\xi\}$ is open in $X_s$. Let $U\subseteq X$ and $V\subseteq S$ be open subsets whose open subschemes are affine, $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], such that $x\in U$ and $f(U)\subseteq V$; let $\varphi:R\to A$ be the ring map induced by $f$ and $\mathfrak q\subset A$ the prime ideal corresponding to $x$. Then $\varphi$ is of finite type and $R\to A$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, (2) implies (4): last paragraph of the proof, lines 3723-3726; finite type of R -> A by Lemma Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), line 2673

proof.text: Use Scheme.Hom.finiteType_appLE on the two affine opens to provide the Algebra.FiniteType instance for the induced section-ring algebra. This is the affine-pair characterization [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs].

Apply Mathlib Scheme.Hom.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_asFiber backwards to the given isolated fibre point. Apply Scheme.Hom.QuasiFiniteAt.quasiFiniteAt to the affine pair and its point to obtain Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt for the induced ring map at the corresponding prime. Apply Algebra.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_fiber forwards to obtain openness of that prime singleton in the topological fibre of the map of spectra. All three are proved Mathlib declarations in Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.QuasiFinite and Mathlib.RingTheory.ZariskisMainTheorem.

The homeomorphism PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-spec-homeomorphism] carries the singleton in the topological fibre to the canonical fibre-ring prime singleton. Rewrite the image of a singleton and use Homeomorph.isOpen_image. By [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], this is exactly the required predicate. Pair it with the finite-type witness from step 1.
